newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan parties, government sign election accord.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan parties, government sign election accord.

text.p: The Moroccan government and 12 political parties with seats in parliament, including the opposition, signed an agreement on Friday to help ensure planned elections take place fairly and honestly.
The accord commits the government to "oppose any illegal interference on the part of any administration" and prevent any abuse of power or illegal use of funds.

The parties on their side agreed to ... "respect the law and all the rules and provisions set jointly with the government within the frame of consensus" ... and not to ... "allow judiciary appeals aimed at casting doubt on the regularity of the electoral operations."
Supreme Court President Driss Dahak, at a signing ceremony with Interior Minister Driss Basri and the party leaders, termed the accord "an historic event".
Under a "Code of Honour" incorporated in the agreement, the two sides agree to ensure candidates do not use illegal funds or try to get the backing of state officials during electioneering.

"Access to public audiovisual means will be allowed to all political parties and trade unions during the campaigns for the general, communal, professional and legislative elections, (in) keeping with the principle of equality and equity..," the code states.
Morocco is expecting fresh elections this year after more than 10 million electors voted 'yes' last September 13 to King Hassan's proposal to split the present 333-seat parliament into two chambers.
The lower house will be elected directly and the upper house indirectly. The second house will have power to force a vote of no-confidence in the government.
Morocco's main opposition parties, the old-guard Istiqlal and Socialist Union of People's Forces, both called for a 'yes' vote in the referendum.
